questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: When a player gives a resource to an NPC who cannot pay, the NPC unlocks a blueprint. No immediate reward.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: npc_social — the mechanical heart of the Mirror of Erised.

questions.q: What would break if this feature did not exist?
questions.a: The Mirror would have no mechanical expression. Giving would have no consequence.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: SacrificeLogComponent and StarMemorialComponent.

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Sub-rung of npc_social.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: Giving consumes resource from inventory. NPC need transitions NEEDING to SATISFIED. Blueprint flag set.

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: Giving player has blueprint unlock that non-giving player does not.

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: No immediate UI reward. No XP, no currency, no notification.

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: All blueprints unlocked on session start, bypassing giving mechanic.

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: Players unlock blueprints without giving, or giving has no effect.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Individual encounter. One player, one NPC, one resource, one unlock.

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Single boolean flag per blueprint per playthrough. Not a skill tree.

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Yes: need detection, transfer animation, unlock propagation.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: After exactly one successful give and check cycle.

questions.q: What would deep enough look like for this feature?
questions.a: Player identifies need, gives resource, verifies unlock at fabricator, beacon changes. No UI text.

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: SacrificeLogComponent entries, InventoryTradeComponent unlock flags, blueprint DataTable.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist in the catalog?
questions.a: ~126 social, ~474 narrative, ~13221 economy.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes but sparse. Key variables are boolean flags.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING from the catalog?
questions.a: Blueprint unlocked via NPC help flag type. Trade commodities exist but not social unlock flags.

questions.q: Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: No. Boolean flag manipulation, not physics simulation.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: DIRECTLY. This IS the mechanical heart. Giving to one who cannot pay is the only unlock.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror?
questions.a: Direct. This sub-rung IS the cost-meaning link.

questions.q: Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
questions.a: No. No mechanical difference between generous and costless. Mirror becomes words, not physics.

questions.q: Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
questions.a: Yes if same resource given multiple times with no deduction. Wall: one unlock per resource type per playthrough.

questions.q: What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
questions.a: Player gives last oxygen can. Hours later at fabricator: Oxygen Recycler blueprint. Recognized without being told.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: SacrificeLog, fabricator_economy, beacon_narrative, inventory.

questions.q: What could break at the seam?
questions.a: Fabricator checks wrong flag name. Blueprint stays locked even after giving.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step?
questions.a: No. NPCs are already placed. Decoder sets need state and unlock table.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: Player gives, NPC satisfied, fabricator has nothing. Player feels cheated.

questions.q: Does this need human judgment?
questions.a: System verifies mechanical loop. Human judges whether it feels meaningful.

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: 5-10. Small boolean parameter space.

questions.q: What population size?
Risk of overfitting?
questions.a: Low. Wall is a simple boolean check.

questions.q: Risk of underfitting?
questions.a: None. Wall is binary: flag set or not.

questions.q: Does the trainer support this?
questions.a: Yes but domain needs hand-authoring. Measure function needs MCP calls for give→unlock test.

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough?
questions.a: At flag level yes. Depth is in FEEL, which is human-judged.

questions.q: What is the next decomposition level?
questions.a: Animation states, particle effects, sound design for the give moment.

questions.q: If we stopped here, would the game feel complete?
questions.a: Loop works but feels empty. Needs animation/audio/VFX to land.

questions.q: What is the expected emotional response?
questions.a: I sacrificed something real and it mattered. I discovered it later, not told.

questions.q: Does this exist because the Mirror demands it?
questions.a: Absolutely. Without it the game has no soul.
